# Requirements

Index the half of a codebase the parser cannot see. Symbols, calls, and routes are the structure graph; purpose, contract, danger, and coupling are the intent graph, and the intent graph lives only in prose. Codify already lexes every comment in 19 languages inside clean_line and then discards them. Capture them as first-class nodes bound to symbols, resolve the names inside them into edges no static analysis can derive, serve them as a survey tier an agent reads before paying for bodies, and use snapshot diffs to keep them honest.

## Requirement 1: Comment capture

**User Story:** As the indexer, I want every comment recorded and classified so that intent becomes queryable without a second parse.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a file is indexed THE scan SHALL record each comment span with its file, start line, end line, and text, taken from the existing cross-line stripper pass.
2. WHEN a comment immediately precedes a definition THE comment SHALL be classified doc and bound to that symbol's id.
3. WHEN a comment opens a file before any definition THE comment SHALL be classified file.
4. WHEN a comment sits inside a symbol's extent THE comment SHALL be classified inline and bound to the enclosing symbol.
5. WHEN comments are captured THE full-repository index time SHALL stay within 10 percent of the pre-capture baseline and SHALL add no link-time dependency.
6. WHEN a captured comment is an anchor — a file header or a doc — or a multi-line note THE text SHALL be matchable by word in a prose index separate from body_fts.
7. WHEN a captured comment is a single-line note inside a symbol THE span SHALL still be stored and bound, and SHALL stay out of the prose index, where a label would dilute retrieval and cost a fifth of the index budget.

## Requirement 2: Doc-first retrieval

**User Story:** As an agent, I want a symbol's intent before its boilerplate so that the same budget buys more understanding.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a symbol carries a doc comment THE snippet SHALL lead with that comment and the signature rather than the first body lines.
2. WHEN a symbol carries no doc comment THE snippet SHALL fall back to the existing body-line behaviour unchanged.
3. WHEN context renders under a fixed budget THE doc-first form SHALL fit strictly more distinct symbols than the body-first form for the same query.
4. WHEN a bound doc comment is stale THE render SHALL mark it stale rather than present it as current.
5. WHEN a doc comment exceeds the per-symbol share of the budget THE render SHALL truncate it and announce the truncation.

## Requirement 3: The survey tier

**User Story:** As a main agent, I want to survey a wide area for the price of one body read so that exploration stops being delegated to sub-agents.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN cg survey runs over a path or a query THE output SHALL contain file purpose lines and symbol docs with signatures and SHALL NOT contain symbol bodies.
2. WHEN survey covers a directory THE per-file cost SHALL stay bounded so that at least one hundred files fit inside the default budget.
3. WHEN a file or a symbol carries no anchor THE survey SHALL name it as uncovered rather than omit it silently.
4. WHEN the budget elides entries THE survey SHALL report an explicit omitted count.
5. WHEN survey is invoked over MCP THE same output SHALL be exposed as a tool.

## Requirement 4: Soft edges

**User Story:** As an agent, I want the couplings a parser cannot see so that cross-language and dynamic relationships stop costing a search.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an anchor comment names a symbol that exists THE indexer SHALL record a reference of kind soft attributed to the symbol the comment is bound to.
2. WHEN a soft edge is traversed or printed THE output SHALL label it soft so that it is never presented as a parsed call.
3. WHEN an anchor names a repository path or a route that exists THE edge SHALL resolve to that file or route.
4. WHEN a name in a comment matches no symbol, path, or route THE indexer SHALL record nothing rather than invent an edge.
5. WHEN cg impact runs THE soft edges SHALL be included and attributed as soft, and excludable by flag.

## Requirement 5: Anchor honesty

**User Story:** As a reviewer, I want stale anchors surfaced so that the intent layer degrades loudly instead of lying quietly.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a bound symbol's body changes and the text of its doc comment does not THE anchor SHALL be marked stale.
2. WHEN the text of an anchor comment changes THE anchor SHALL re-baseline against the current symbol body and clear its stale mark.
3. WHEN retrieval ranks anchors THE stale anchors SHALL rank below current ones.
4. WHEN cg guard runs over uncommitted work THE anchors that work made stale SHALL be reported as warnings and SHALL NOT block.
5. WHEN cg check runs THE stale anchor count SHALL be reported as part of its summary.

## Requirement 6: The anchor convention

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want a stated contract and a way to find gaps so that anchors get written where they pay and nowhere else.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the convention is documented THE four anchor kinds — purpose, contract, danger, pointer — SHALL be stated together with the derivability test that excludes any comment restating the code.
2. WHEN cg anchors ranks uncovered symbols THE ranking SHALL use a coordination score — fan-out times extent times distinct referencing files — and SHALL NOT use raw inbound reference count, which ranks self-evident utilities highest.
3. WHEN a repository has never adopted the convention THE capture, retrieval, survey, and edge features SHALL still function on whatever comments already exist.
4. WHEN the convention ships THE agent instructions SHALL carry it and the workflow spec SHALL name anchors as part of the loop.
